title: Understanding AL Development: Environmental Information Code Unit
summary: Codeunit 457 Environment Information provides methods to detect deployment type, environment type, and application family in AL extensions. It helps developers run different code paths for production versus sandbox environments, such as redirecting emails in sandbox to safe addresses instead of real clients.
key_points: Codeunit 457 Environment Information exposes methods like IsProduction, IsSandbox, IsSaaS, IsOnPrem, and IsFinancials to check environment characteristics
IsProduction and IsSandbox are useful for gating operations, such as skipping email sends or redirecting to test addresses in sandbox
IsSaaSInfrastructure distinguishes between SaaS infrastructure hosting and Docker testing environments, returning false in Docker
CanStartSession checks if a new session can be started via Session.StartSession for multi-session processing
Common use case is preventing sensitive operations like sending remittance notices to real customers when a production environment copy exists in sandbox

quotes.text: There are cases where we want some different behavior depending on specific environmental details.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why developers need to detect and respond to environment differences in their code

quotes.text: If someone makes a copy of the Production environment to a Sandbox, we want to change this behavior.
quotes.why_it_matters: Illustrates the critical security use case of preventing unintended operations like sending real emails from sandbox copies

quotes.text: This is a great little code unit which can be useful in helping you manage your code execution.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the practical value of Environment Information for controlling extension behavior across different deployment scenarios
